text: Marjane Satrapi's Persepolis: The Story of a Childhood was challenged repeatedly. In March 2013, administrators at Chicago Public Schools' Fullerton school network and Lane Tech High School directed its removal from school libraries and classrooms, citing inappropriate language and images; CPS Chief Barbara Byrd Bennett later limited the directive to seventh-grade classrooms. A parent in Oregon's Three Rivers School District sought its removal from high school libraries over "coarse language and scenes of torture", but it was retained without restriction. A parent in central Illinois' Ball-Chatham School District then called it inappropriate for the senior-level English students assigned to read it. On February 17, 2014, a formal challenge at Smithville High School went before the school board, which voted 5-1 to retain the book. In June 2015, a college student and her parents said it should be "eradicated from the system" at Crafton Hills College in Yucaipa, California.
meta_description: Persepolis by Marjane Satrapi: removal directed in Chicago schools in March 2013, retained in Oregon and at Smithville in 2014, challenged in 2015.
